data.title: Collection notice ("last warning before seizure") from EuroClaim Forderungsmanagement Ltd.
data.summary: EuroClaim Forderungsmanagement Ltd., a debt-collection company based in Limassol, Cyprus, demands 287.40 EUR for an alleged telephone "Lotto-Muster-Club" subscription debt, to be paid within 72 hours (by 06.08.2026) to a foreign trustee account, threatening account seizure, a negative SCHUFA entry and a criminal complaint if unpaid.
data.explanation: This letter shows several classic warning signs of a scam collection notice: an extremely short 72-hour deadline, a payment account held by a private individual abroad instead of a German business account, fees that are disproportionate to the claimed debt, and a statement discouraging you from objecting — none of which fit how legitimate German debt collectors normally operate. Do not transfer any money before verifying the claim. Check whether you ever concluded such a subscription, ask the named "client" for proof, and consider contacting a consumer protection agency (Verbraucherzentrale) or a lawyer before responding. Genuine legal consequences like account seizure require a court order, not a private letter.

items.title: Pay disputed collection demand
items.action: Verify the underlying claim before paying; the letter demands payment to a foreign trustee account within a very short deadline.
items.consequence: Otherwise the sender threatens account seizure (Kontopfändung), a negative SCHUFA entry, and a criminal complaint for 'Eingehungsbetrug' without further notice.
items.quote: Überweisen Sie den Gesamtbetrag innerhalb von 72 Stunden, spätestens bis 06.08.2026, ausschließlich auf folgendes Treuhandkonto: IBAN LT71 7300 0101 2345 6789, Kontoinhaber: A. Petrauskas, Verwendungszweck EC-DE-2026-481120.

warnings: This has multiple hallmarks of a debt-collection scam: a foreign trustee account held by a private individual (not the company) rather than a normal business account, disproportionate fees relative to the alleged principal, and an unusually short 72-hour deadline.
The letter explicitly discourages you from objecting ('Ein Widerspruch ist zwecklos'), which is a manipulation tactic, not a legal fact — you always retain the right to dispute a claim.

Threats of immediate account seizure, a SCHUFA entry and criminal prosecution without any prior court proceeding are not how genuine debt enforcement works in Germany and should be treated as pressure tactics.
Do not transfer money to the given IBAN or reply with personal/financial data before independently verifying the claim, e.g. via a consumer protection agency (Verbraucherzentrale) or a lawyer.
data.case_title: Suspicious collection demand from EuroClaim Forderungsmanagement (Lotto-Muster-Club subscription)
